sections.h2: Choosing the quickest way to sell in Troy
sections.html:
Troy sellers can price a listing to draw several bids, line up a buyer on their own, or accept cash from a buyer who asks for no repairs. Home values in Troy run high for the area, so weeks of prep can earn real money, but cash fits an owner short on time.

Owners' median home value is $420,300 and median household income is $120,045 for 2020 through 2024. Buyers at that price read inspection reports closely. Heavy repairs, an estate or a job move can steer a seller to one offer from a buyer who takes on the work.

  • Agent listing: suits a house in good shape and a seller who can live with inspection and lender timelines.
  • Private sale: possible if you can produce a contract and a deed that the county will accept.
  • Cash offer: fits when speed, privacy or the house's condition outweighs getting the highest price.

In Oakland County, Troy covers 33.45 square miles of land, borders Sterling Heights to the east, and has an estimated 88,733 residents as of mid-2025, up from 87,294 in 2020. Troy incorporated as a city in 1955. In ZIP code 48098 the January average low is 22 degrees Fahrenheit and precipitation totals near 32 inches a year, which is why inspectors check roofs and gutters carefully.

Big Beaver Road anchors the business district, with the Somerset Collection mall and the Oakland Mall nearby. Retail sales reached $4.17 billion in 2022, about $47,709 per resident, so shopping and jobs sit close to most neighborhoods.

About 34.4% of residents speak a second language at home, which makes clear photos and plain written terms worth the effort.

Seven districts divide Troy. The home district for most addresses is Troy School District, with twelve elementary schools, four middle schools, Troy High and Athens High, plus the International Academy's eastern campus. Elementary buildings inside the city also belong to Avondale, Birmingham and Warren Consolidated, while Bloomfield Hills, Royal Oak and Lamphere cover small areas.

Neighbors may attend different districts, so put the district in your listing, and verify any address close to a boundary.

Troy's assessor sets assessed value at half of market value. That office also handles the Principal Residence Exemption and the Property Transfer Affidavit.

  • Summer bill: goes out July 1 and is clear of penalty through September 1. A 4% charge follows, with half a percent monthly starting October 1.
  • Winter bill: goes out December 1 and is clear through February 14, followed by 3%.
  • On March 1, open current-year balances shift to the Oakland County Treasurer at 248.858.0611, option 7.

Troy collects for seven school districts plus the county, Oakland Schools, Macomb Intermediate and several county authorities. School levies change with the district and with principal-residence status, so look-alike houses can get different bills. An owner who is 62 or older or disabled, with income at or under $40,000, can apply through September 15 to defer payment to April 30.

A sale lifts the cap on the buyer's taxable value starting the next calendar year. Prorations are set by contract, and call the Treasurer's Office at 248.524.3333 to learn what is due on a given date. The Assessor, Clerk and Treasurer all work out of City Hall at 500 W. Big Beaver Road, which usually lets you finish records and tax errands in one visit.

sections.h2: Transfer tax and the Oakland County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
State law puts the transfer tax on the seller, payable within 15 days after the deed is delivered (MCL 207.523). The state's piece is $3.75 for every $500 (MCL 207.525), and the county's piece is 55 cents per $500 for counties under 2,000,000 residents (MCL 207.504). Check the Oakland County figure with the register before you close.

Reach the Register of Deeds at 248-858-0597 or deeds@oaklandcountymi.gov on weekdays; the counter opens at 8:30 a.m. Deeds, mortgages and foreclosure records are filed there, and the Super Index can retrieve recorded documents dating to January 1, 1964.

MCL 207.526 exempts gifts to children and grandchildren, foreclosure deeds and court orders that state no price. The deed itself has to cite the exemption.

sections.h2: Yard and property rules to settle before showings
sections.html:
Troy's Code Enforcement office posts the complaints it fields most. A single walk around the property before the first showing can save you a violation notice mid-listing.

  • Grass and weeds must stay below 8 inches between May 1 and October 31, including the strip to the road.
  • Sidewalk snow over 2 inches and any ice must be cleared within 24 hours of a storm.
  • Vehicles kept on private land must carry current plates and run, and RVs cannot sit on the street.
  • Temporary signs are allowed on private property, while signs in the public right-of-way are removed.
  • Put bins out only after 5 p.m. the evening before pickup, and trim branches over sidewalks up to 8 feet.

Put open house and yard signs on your own lot only. Two more rules matter to some sellers: one commercial pickup or cargo van may sit on private property in a one-family district, and home businesses are allowed in one- and two-family districts under conditions, so a buyer planning to work from the house should call Code Enforcement first.

Begin with taxes: find out from the Treasurer's Office where your bill stands and how proration would work on your planned closing date. Check the yard against the list above. Take offers in writing, and have each bidder name a closing date and say who covers transfer tax. A cash buyer has no lender appraisal holding things up, so timing depends mostly on title work and the deed. After you accept, the title company drafts the deed, confirms the transfer tax and sends it to the Register of Deeds.

Hand the title company your payoff letter, a recent tax bill and permit records, and mention right away if the deed qualifies for an exemption. A buyer who intends to rent the house or run a business from it should talk to Code Enforcement before closing. Request a written closing statement from the title company showing the tax proration, the transfer tax and the recording fee, and compare every line to your contract before you sign. If anything looks off, raise it with the title company before closing day, since fixing a figure afterward takes longer.

faqs.q: What is a typical Troy home worth?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes had a median value of $420,300 in 2020 to 2024, though age, lot and district move individual prices.

faqs.q: When do Troy tax bills come due?
faqs.a: You can pay the summer bill through September 1 and the winter bill through February 14. Balances still open on March 1 move to Oakland County.

faqs.q: Do Troy taxes reset after I sell?
faqs.a: For the buyer they can. A transfer of ownership lifts the cap on taxable value the following calendar year.

faqs.q: Which school district is a Troy house in?
faqs.a: Troy School District covers most houses. Avondale, Birmingham, Bloomfield Hills, Lamphere, Royal Oak and Warren Consolidated each serve some areas.

faqs.q: Where is a Troy deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Oakland County Register of Deeds, 248-858-0597. The deed pays transfer tax unless it names an exemption.
